prompt: help me plan out how to get good at chess. im around 800 elo on lichess rapid right now. goal is to hit 1500 by end of the year — its april so thats 8-9 months. i can realistically do 30-45 min a day most days. i know basic rules and very basic tactics (pins, forks, that kinda thing). i have no idea what to actually spend my time on — should i be doing puzzles, playing games, studying openings, watching streamers, reading a book, something else? whats the actual plan

assertions.text: Includes a concrete daily session structure with time allocations (minutes per activity)
Includes a phased roadmap with named milestones tied to rating or skill markers
Prioritizes tactics/puzzles heavily, appropriate for the 800-1500 band
Deprioritizes openings / warns against opening-theory rabbit holes at 800 ELO
Recommends slower time controls (rapid / classical) over blitz/bullet for learning
Includes post-game analysis / reviewing losses as a core practice
Includes spaced / distributed review of previously-seen positions or missed puzzles
Emphasizes active production (solving puzzles, calculating) over passive consumption (streamers, videos)
Names specific resources (books, courses, or tools) rather than vague pointers
Warns about common failure modes tailored to this rating (e.g., blitz tilt, opening obsession, streamer-watching)
Warns that the plan will feel slower/harder than intuitive approaches (desirable difficulty)
Includes a feedback mechanism for identifying specific weaknesses to drill
